context: Inventory every authoritative and derived platform surface before choosing ownership. Separate static metadata needed before imports from runtime adapter objects. Reuse the existing registry/decorator boundary, derive deterministic outputs only where they have durable consumers, and encode intentional surface differences as typed metadata rather than undocumented exceptions.
description: Platform identity and support metadata is repeated across registry, aliases, CLI choices, documentation, and validation surfaces. Establish a single typed manifest or an explicitly generated static projection while preserving lazy SDK imports. The manifest, generated outputs, consistency tests, and required drift gate must land together so the new source of truth cannot immediately diverge.

anti_patterns.dont: Add a manifest that duplicates an equally authoritative registry.
anti_patterns.instead: Declare one authority and make every other surface derived or validated.
anti_patterns.why: Two sources of truth worsen the original drift problem.

anti_patterns.dont: Instantiate adapters to obtain static metadata.
anti_patterns.instead: Store import-safe static facts separately from runtime objects.
anti_patterns.why: That breaks lazy imports and increases discovery cost.

anti_patterns.dont: Land generated outputs without the drift gate.
anti_patterns.instead: Land source generation and required validation atomically.
anti_patterns.why: The outputs can become stale immediately.

preserves.behavior: Existing platform keys aliases and CLI spellings remain compatible unless separately deprecated.
Generated outputs are deterministic and reviewed alongside their source.
Optional platform SDKs are not imported during manifest or registry enumeration.
PlatformAdapter plus @register_platform remains the runtime registration invariant.

verifications.expected: This command exits nonzero when a platform alias or registry entry is removed from only one surface and exits zero when derived surfaces agree.
